## 1. Verdict

**The single first blocker is NOT code. It is the guest-side remote-management path of
`windows-utm-1`:**

1. The UTM guest (`Windows11`, UUID `3FEF5C3F-43A3-4251-B767-319786870F90`) is **powered off**
   today (2026-09-03, `utmctl list`), and even when booted it had **no reachable management
   path**: 2026-08-28 health check (`WindowsNodeBootstrapTriageVerdict_2026-08-28.md` §6) —
   ICMP ok, RPC/NetBIOS/SMB open, but **TCP/22, 3389 and 5985 all CLOSED**, no QEMU guest agent.
   The `--node` orchestrator drives Windows guests exclusively over
   PowerShell-over-SSH (`guest_exec_mode: windows_powershell`, inventory entry `windows-utm-1`,
   `remote_shell: powershell`), so `bootstrap_hosts` cannot even be attempted.
2. Live probes 2026-09-03 (this machine): `192.168.64.25:22` closed/timeout, `:5985`
   closed/timeout, ARP `(incomplete)` on bridge100 — consistent with guest powered off.
   `windows-x86-1` (`192.168.121.108` on `ubuntu-kvm-1`): :22/:5985 closed — its host
   `ubuntu-kvm-1` has been unreachable since ≥2026-08-28 (PassLikelihood doc §2), so that guest
   is equally unavailable.

## 2. Is it code-fixable or environment/hardware?

**Environment/ops.** There is no known code change that moves a Windows guest one stage further
from this machine: the orchestrator cannot open a shell to a guest that is powered off and has
no listening management port. Conversely, the bootstrap path itself is, on paper, ready:

- `winget configure` is a **cold-guest-only** branch (`-Phase build-release` only,
  `windows_install.rs:575`; guarded by a toolchain-presence check) — and it is the branch
  W-FIX-1 self-heals. Note this branch never ran in the bash era (its 66 bootstrap passes rode
  pre-baked toolchains), which is why bash-era greens are not evidence (PassLikelihood §3.1).
- WinNAT/exit hardware (CP-3) and the DPAPI / named-pipe / WFP capabilities gate **downstream
  cells, not `bootstrap_hosts`** (PassLikelihood §3.3/§3.4): the client bootstrap cell needs
  none of them.
- Known **post-bootstrap** walls, so the first green is planned as "run once and triage", not
  "make it green": (a) the §4.7 identity gate — `enforce_identity_challenge`
  (`node_adapter.rs:516-524`) fails closed every validator-backed Windows stage; NOTE the
  PassLikelihood doc's "no Windows `status` subcommand" root cause was **REFUTED** by
  `LiveLabStagePassLikelihoodSummaryAdversarialReview_2026-09-01.md` (candidate 1): the live
  surface already exists end to end (`role status` → `IpcCommand::Status` → daemon replies
  `node_id=`/`node_role=` key=value), so the remaining work is consuming the existing response
  field, not building a subcommand; (b) CP-1-class LAN reachability has never
  been measured for a Windows guest (`windows-utm-1` sits on the same 192.168.64.x Shared-NAT
  fabric where macOS cross-node traffic has no L3 path).
